subject: OrbitPay overnight P2 latency — temporary response exemption request
messages:
From: Mike Thornton <mike.thornton@orbitpay.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Cc: Emma Li <emma.li@orbitpay.com>
Date: Mon, 3 Nov 2025 04:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: production latency spike overnight — P2 response window

Evelyn,

Quick note from the overnight ops shift — between 02:10 and 03:05 PST on 2025-11-02 we saw repeated P2 alerts tied to tokenization/latency regressions against the Redwood hosted endpoints. The throttling and burstback helped, but our payments queue backed up and we had to fall back to a degraded path for ~35 minutes.

This is the second night this month with sustained P2s during the 00:00–04:00 window. Our SRE lead (Emma) asked I connect with you to request a temporary SLO amendment for the night window while we work through your suggested model pin and cache profile changes. Specifically: a temporary P2 response SLA exemption (wider response window) for 00:00–04:30 PST for 7 days, with a mutually agreed escalation ladder and a credit adjustment if the incident recurs beyond that window.

Attachments: orbitpay-slo-impact-log-20251102.csv (csv) — full alert timeline and traces.

We want to keep production stable and are OK with the exemption only if you can confirm an internal plan (on-call shifts, runbook steps) to prevent P1 regressions. Can you confirm next steps and a timeline?

Thanks,
Mike Thornton\Director of Platform Engineering\OrbitPay
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
To: Mike Thornton <mike.thornton@orbitpay.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 3 Nov 2025 07:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: production latency spike overnight — P2 response window

Mike — thanks for the detail and the log. I’m sorry you hit this again. We’ve reviewed the CSV and the traces; the pattern looks tied to a recent batch rollout + cache warming on the model variant you’re pinned to.

Short answer: we can support a temporary P2 window amendment for the 00:00–04:30 PST block for seven evenings, but we need a concrete mitigation plan and an agreed escalation path first (to ensure P1s are routed and staffed).

Proposed immediate actions (we’ll follow up with an internal runbook and on-call staffing):
- Ben will set up a canary that pins a slightly older quantized variant for the 00:00–04:30 window to reduce latency risk.
- Karthik will confirm on-call overlap coverage and add a 1hr shadow between 23:30–00:30 for the next three nights.
- We’ll commit to daily notes and one post-mortem if the exemption is used and a P1 occurs.

If that sounds OK, I’ll draft the temporary SLO amendment and the escalation ladder for sign-off (and include your requested credit clause).

Evelyn Hart\Senior Customer Reliability Manager\Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>, Mike Thornton <mike.thornton@orbitpay.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 3 Nov 2025 08:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: production latency spike overnight — P2 response window

On the technical side — quick notes and an ops tweak I can implement tonight: 

1) Canary variant: I’ll schedule a variant pin for OrbitPay’s route that slides to v1.3-q8 (previous stable) between 23:58–04:35 PST. This addresses the tail-latency we saw after the batch push.
2) Cache priming: I’ll preload the KV cache for the 4 highest-volume prefixes (based on your CSV) immediately before the window. That should reduce the cold-start amplification.
3) Autoscaler floor: Increasing the minimal replica count by 1 for that capacity pool during the window; this buys headroom if we see burst retries.

I’ll attach a short checklist (proposed-temporary-slo-amendment-orbitpay.pdf) to the SLO proposal. Note: these changes are low-risk and reversible; if we detect any P1 indicators we rollback the canary and engage the P1 path.

Ben Carter\Principal SRE, Redwood Inference\Attachment: proposed-temporary-slo-amendment-orbitpay.pdf (pdf)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 4 Nov 2025 01:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: production latency spike overnight — P2 response window

Adding on-call staffing detail and the escalation ladder we’ll follow if the exemption is enacted: 

- Night shadow: I will allocate an on-call engineer (internal rotation) to shadow OrbitPay between 23:30–00:30 PST for the next three nights.
- Response ladder for the temporary window:
  * P2 during 00:00–04:30: night responder (target 90m acknowledgement, 180m mitigation) — this is the temporary softened window.
  * Any sign of increased error rate or queue growth triggers immediate escalation to P1 routing (Pager to mobile, 15m ack target).
  * If P1 routes, we automatically abort the exemption and engage SRE & CS on-call plus an on-call engineering manager.
- Communication: We’ll send a nightly short-status (end-of-window) to your ops channel and a consolidated note to your stakeholders after the 7-day window.

I’ll also post the runbook snippet to the shared Drive (link in the metadata). Ben — confirm you’re OK with the canary schedule and the autoscaler floor change.

—Karthik\Karthik Iyer\Director, Incident Response\Redwood Inference
From: Mike Thornton <mike.thornton@orbitpay.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Cc: Emma Li <emma.li@orbitpay.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 5 Nov 2025 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: production latency spike overnight — P2 response window

Thanks — that plan reads reasonable. Two quick asks before we confirm the exemption: 
1) Can you add the exact rollback trigger thresholds (queue depth > 5000, 5xx rate > 0.8% sustained 5m) into the runbook? We want deterministic abort conditions.
2) Can you confirm the credit mechanism if the same class of P2 recurs after the 7-day window? OrbitPay would look for a pro-rated credit for the affected hours unless a P1 occurred that would void the credit.

If you can reply with those details I’ll sign off from our side and we can start tonight’s canary at 23:58 PST. Appreciate the fast coordination.

Mike Thornton\Director of Platform Engineering\OrbitPay
